name: copy_nonoverlapping
declaration: const unsafe fn copy_nonoverlapping < T > (src : * const T , dst : * mut T , count : usize)
rules: `src` must be valid for reads of `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes. For a nonzero byte count, this requires a non-null pointer whose entire accessed range lies within the allocated object determined by its provenance; these conditions alone are not necessarily sufficient for validity.

`dst` must be valid for writes of `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes. For a nonzero byte count, this requires a non-null pointer whose entire accessed range lies within the allocated object determined by its provenance; these conditions alone are not necessarily sufficient for validity.
`src` must be aligned to `align_of::<T>()`, even when `count * size_of::<T>()` is zero.
`dst` must be aligned to `align_of::<T>()`, even when `count * size_of::<T>()` is zero.
The region beginning at `src` of length `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes must not overlap the region beginning at `dst` of the same length.
When `count * size_of::<T>()` is zero, every pointer, including a null or dangling pointer, satisfies the read/write validity requirement; both pointers must still be aligned to `align_of::<T>()`.
The copied data may be uninitialized or otherwise violate the validity requirements of `T`; `copy_nonoverlapping` does not require the data to be valid values of `T`.
`copy_nonoverlapping` preserves the initialization state of the copied bytes exactly.
`T` need not implement `Copy` for this operation to be permitted. If `T` does not implement `Copy`, using both the source values and their destination copies is not guaranteed to be memory-safe.
The reads and writes performed by `copy_nonoverlapping` are non-atomic: concurrent accesses from another thread to the same locations are undefined behavior unless both accesses only read memory.

A pointer obtained by casting a reference is guaranteed valid for the relevant access while the underlying object remains live and no reference is used to access the same memory; reference accesses and raw-pointer accesses must not be interleaved.
